english.title: Holder of manufacturing authorisation fail to have at his disposal the services of a qualified person

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for human use clinical trials regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the holder of a manufacturing authorisation, failed to have at your disposal the services of at least one qualified person who was responsible for carrying out the duties referred to in regulation 43(2) of the the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 43(1), 49(1)(m) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

subject to reg 43(4) / 43(5)

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 49 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 makes a breach of reg 43 an offence.
(ii) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides that a person does not commit an offence under these Regulations if he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of that offence. Where evidence is adduced which is sufficient to raise an issue with respect to that defence, the court or jury shall assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.
(iii) Regulation 43(2) provides that a qualified person shall be responsible for carrying out the duties specified in Article 13(3) and (4) of the Directive, in accordance with that Article, in respect of the investigational medicinal products manufactured, assembled or imported in accordance with the authorisation in question.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
